summary: Quick postmortem focused on access blockers (VPC peering, gateway NATs), a small but persistent latency variance in staging runs, and next steps to enable a hosted fallback while infra teams clear the VPC handoff. Security asked for explicit docs and a walkthrough of KMS/SAML flow.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-29 10:30 PT
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (BlueWave VP Eng), Samir Patel (BlueWave SRE), Dana Brooks (BlueWave Head of Security), Evan Li (BlueWave ML)

Summary: quick troubleshooting and alignment on infra blockers, agreement to run hosted fallback and capture traces, action items assigned.

00:00:12 - Alex Chen: okay starting, hi everyone thanks for joining our garage hour postmortem, i think we only have ~40 minutes.
00:00:28 - Marta Alvarez: yep thanks Alex, we wanted to get unblocked for the POC -- main stuck points were peering and some odd 95th-percentile spikes we saw in the staging run.
00:00:47 - Priya Kapoor: right, thanks Marta. i pulled the traces earlier, there's a mix of gateway NAT timeouts and an unexpected retry path when the kv cache returns empty.
00:01:05 - Samir Patel: to clarify, the test run we did at 8am used the staging gateway; we saw median ~60ms but p95 up to 300ms on a few requests, and some TLS handshake delays.
00:01:22 - Priya Kapoor: hm that matches what i saw, there's a small window where our client retries at 2x backoff which amplifies latency. could be due to MTU on the peered link or a firewall rule doing deep inspection.
00:01:41 - Dana Brooks: from security side we locked down the peering strictly; we can open inspection for the POC but need to document. we also need to see KMS key rotation plan, and a SAML flow diagram.
00:02:02 - Alex Chen: understood, we can provide the KMS diagram and key lifecycle notes. quick question Marta, who owns the cloud egress rules?
00:02:14 - Marta Alvarez: samir does but evan's team touched the VPC earlier. samir?
00:02:19 - Samir Patel: yes we control egress; i can toggle packet capture tomorrow if that helps. i'm worried about exposing anything sensitive so we'll do limited-duration captures.
00:02:34 - Priya Kapoor: packet captures would be super useful. also, i'll re-run with increased kv cache prefixes so fewer cache misses — that should reduce retries.
00:02:49 - Evan Li: can you explain the kv cache prefix change? we didn't change anything on our end.
00:02:55 - Priya Kapoor: sure — some of your prompt families have different initial tokens, which leads to cold starts in the prefix cache; increasing prefix window groups those requests, so the runtime can reuse KV cache entries.
00:03:10 - Evan Li: ah ok makes sense.
00:03:16 - Alex Chen: stepping back on the operability question, we should decide temporary path: either keep pushing VPC peering fix or use Redwood hosted fallback for the next round of benchmarks. thoughts?
00:03:31 - Marta Alvarez: hosted fallback is fine for initial performance validation as long as data isn't persisted beyond the session and we have assurance about region and encryption.
00:03:44 - Dana Brooks: we need KMS integration or envelope encryption to ensure keys are managed — hosted fallback is okay if we use a customer-managed key or we can anonymize payloads.
00:03:58 - Marco Diaz: quick note — for pilots we often do a 'no PII' payload sanitization while infra gates are still closing. that has been acceptable in other health customers.
00:04:12 - Marta Alvarez: that could work, but we still need to see SOC2 docs and the data retention policy.
00:04:21 - Alex Chen: we'll attach SOC2+ISO summary to the email; marco will follow up.

00:05:02 - Priya Kapoor: back to latency, i pulled a flamegraph from the earlier run: the time is spent in two places: TLS handshake at the gateway and a 30-60ms cost on the first token generation when cache miss + quantized model loading overlaps.
00:05:22 - Samir Patel: interesting — could the quantization profile be falling back to a less-opt kernel?
00:05:29 - Priya Kapoor: possible, our runtime chooses kernels based on model size and sequence length. for this POC i suggested a 4-bit profile but if sequence lengths spike above 256 it sometimes triggers a different path.
00:05:42 - Evan Li: our user flows do have occasional long contexts up to 512 for diagnostic prompts.
00:05:48 - Priya Kapoor: okay that's likely the variance source. two mitigations: pin quant profile to a slower but consistent kernel (reduce p95) or proactively chunk prompts smaller.
00:05:59 - Marta Alvarez: pinning seems safer for now. what's impact on cost?
00:06:05 - Priya Kapoor: we'll do a quick cost delta, but expected small increase per token vs unpredictable p95 spikes. i'll include numbers in the perf spreadsheet.

00:07:10 - Dana Brooks: on SSO/SAML, we attempted the metadata exchange yesterday but our IdP rejected a couple of the assertion consumer endpoints. we need a walkthrough.
00:07:24 - Alex Chen: ok we'll pair with you on a SAML test. Marco — can you own that?
00:07:29 - Marco Diaz: yep i'll schedule a 30-min security handshake with Dana and the IdP team next week.
00:07:34 - Alex Chen: thanks.

00:08:00 - Samir Patel: quick infra note — the peering used a /22 from our side overlapping with a vendor CIDR we forgot about; that caused asymmetric routing and some packets got hairpinned to an inspection appliance.
00:08:16 - Priya Kapoor: that explains the MTU/drop patterns. resolving the CIDR overlap should drop a lot of the retries.
00:08:24 - Marta Alvarez: we'll reassign a /23 and cut a change window. can Redwood validate connectivity from your end once we apply?
00:08:33 - Alex Chen: yes we can run a smoke test and synthetic traffic. we'll also enable temporary increased logging.
00:08:41 - Evan Li: one more data point from tests — we saw slightly higher tokenization time for medical terms, probably due to token boundaries. does runtime cache tokenization?
00:08:51 - Priya Kapoor: tokenization is local client-side; we don't modify that. if those terms are common, adding them to a client-side token dictionary helps.
00:08:59 - Evan Li: noted. we'll try that.

00:09:30 - Alex Chen: ok wrapping into a plan: (1) Samir to reassign CIDR and share change window (2) Dana to accept SAML walkthrough invitation (3) Redwood to stand up hosted fallback with envelope encryption and limited retention for perf runs (4) Priya to re-run with kv cache prefix tuning and pinned quant profile.
00:09:55 - Marta Alvarez: that looks good. what's the timeline to see new perf numbers?
00:10:01 - Priya Kapoor: i can run another full pass tomorrow evening after the change window, and share a perf spreadsheet by EOD 2026-09-30.
00:10:09 - Alex Chen: perfect.

00:10:45 - Marco Diaz: on operational notes, we'll also prepare a short runbook for failover: how to flip from VPC routing to hosted fallback and back, and expected DNS / endpoint changes.
00:10:58 - Samir Patel: please make sure the runbook includes rollback steps for firewall and NAT rules.
00:11:05 - Marco Diaz: will do.

00:11:40 - Dana Brooks: returning to compliance, do you support customer-managed KMS in hosted mode? that's a pretty big gating item.
00:11:50 - Alex Chen: yes we support CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) in hosted for pilots in many regions; we'll include the exact regions and the process for key rotation.
00:11:59 - Dana Brooks: good, add that to the doc package.

00:12:20 - Evan Li: small question — if we do hosted fallback, will the model version match what we're testing in dedicated staging?
00:12:28 - Priya Kapoor: we'll pin the same model artifact and quant profile; some low-level kernel choices may differ slightly by hardware but we aim for the same semantic outputs. we'll note any divergence.
00:12:40 - Evan Li: ok helpful.

00:13:10 - Alex Chen: any competitors or alternatives you're evaluating so we can be aware?
00:13:17 - Marta Alvarez: honestly a few infra vendors but nothing concrete; we mentioned Anthropic and Cohere briefly in our vendor review list.
00:13:25 - Alex Chen: thanks, good to know.

00:13:50 - Priya Kapoor: technical ask: Samir, can you provide a short pcap and the tcpdump around the 8am run window? that will help isolate whether it's MTU or a mid-path NAT.
00:14:03 - Samir Patel: yes i can produce a 30-min pcap and scrub IPs as needed. i'll push it to the shared S3 link with time markers.
00:14:11 - Alex Chen: great.

00:14:40 - Marta Alvarez: one process note — our legal team asked for a simple summary of data flows for the POC. they don't need the full T&C but a diagram and retention table.
00:14:53 - Marco Diaz: we can produce a one-page dataflow and retention FAQ and attach SOC2 and ISO summaries.
00:15:02 - Dana Brooks: also include audit log retention and API key rotation cadence.
00:15:07 - Marco Diaz: noted.

00:15:40 - Priya Kapoor: i'll also include the quant/kv suggestions in the perf spreadsheet so you can see expected p95 impact.
00:15:48 - Evan Li: ok thanks Priya.

00:16:10 - Alex Chen: let's capture next steps and owners — i'll read them out and we'll paste into the meeting notes email.
00:16:18 - Alex Chen: action items recap: Alex to share gateway logs and host fallback plan; Priya to rerun with kv/quant pinning and share perf sheet; Marco to schedule SAML walkthrough and produce dataflow doc; Samir to provide pcap and CIDR update; Dana to confirm compliance items.
00:16:43 - Marta Alvarez: timeline sounds good.
00:16:48 - Evan Li: quick last question — on telemetry, do you ingest request IDs so we can correlate traces to our app logs?
00:16:56 - Priya Kapoor: yes we support passing an external request-id header that is reflected in our tracing and logs. we'll show that in the sample trace.
00:17:06 - Alex Chen: we'll attach a sample trace and show how to correlate.

00:17:30 - Marco Diaz: final note — we'll stand up the hosted fallback env on Thursday for a short smoke test, pending CIDR update.
00:17:41 - Marta Alvarez: works for us.
00:17:47 - Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with attached docs and schedule. talk soon.
00:17:56 - (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (auto): transcription has some minor mis-recognitions (product names), speakers were consistent but occasional crosstalk.
notes: Customer is healthcare org; security and KMS are gating items. Agreed hosted fallback while infra resolves CIDR overlap; multiple action items assigned.
duration_outline_fit: transcript covers initial 18 minutes of a 42-min meeting; remaining time was quick Q&A and wrap — notes capture key points.
